question: Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
evidence: league with highest matches of all time refers to MAX(COUNT(league_id));
clarification: Also keep rows that have no matching the joined table record.
gold: SELECT t2.name, t1.max_count FROM League AS t2 LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, MAX(cnt) AS max_count FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(id) AS cnt FROM Match GROUP BY league_id) AS subquery) AS t1 ON t1.league_id = t2.id
gold0: SELECT t2.name, t1.max_count FROM League AS t2 JOIN (SELECT league_id, MAX(cnt) AS max_count FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(id) AS cnt FROM Match GROUP BY league_id) AS subquery) AS t1 ON t1.league_id = t2.id

d.request: Which league has the most matches of all time, and how many matches were played in it? Include rows with no matching record in the joined table.
d.sql: SELECT l.name AS league, COUNT(m.id) AS match_count FROM League AS l LEFT JOIN "Match" AS m ON m.league_id = l.id GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY match_count DESC LIMIT 1;

c.sql: SELECT l.name, COUNT(m.league_id) AS match_count FROM League AS l LEFT JOIN "Match" AS m ON m.league_id = l.id GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY match_count DESC, l.name LIMIT 1;

b.request: Return the league name and match count for the league with the most matches, including leagues with no matching Match records when comparing counts
b.sql: SELECT l.name AS league_name, COUNT(m.id) AS match_count FROM League AS l LEFT JOIN "Match" AS m ON m.league_id = l.id GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY match_count DESC LIMIT 1;
